intro: Match each event to what was going on around it.

right.label: Britain is deep in debt after the French and Indian War and wants the colonies to help pay
The fighting has started, but many colonists still hope to make peace with the king
The states have just fought a war against a king and fear any strong central power
Shays' Rebellion has shown the national government can't keep order
The country fears war with France, and two political parties are attacking each other in print

rationale.a: Thomas Whately (Document 2) says Britain carries a huge debt from a war fought to protect the colonies.
rationale.b: Paine writes against people who say, “Come, come, we shall be friends again” (Document 6). Not everyone wanted independence yet.
rationale.c: The Congress fighting a king built a weak central government on purpose (Document 11).
rationale.d: Farmers shut the Massachusetts courts in 1786–87, and Congress had no force of its own.
rationale.e: Washington warned about parties in 1796. Two years later, with war with France feared, one party passed a law used against the other's editors.

a: What war had just ended, and who paid for it?
b: Paine is arguing with people who still want to be friends with Britain.
Look for hope of peace with the king.
c: Who had the states just been fighting?
Look for fear of strong central power.
d: Look for a rebellion the government couldn't stop.
e: Which country did Americans fear a war with in 1798?
Look for France and political parties.
